title: Autotune: add batching/caching defaults, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers running diverse workloads have different latency/cost sweet spots. This PR implements autotune defaults for batching and caching, introduces curated quantization profiles for common model families, and adds a lightweight unit-econ reporting CLI/dashboard to make tradeoffs visible. Motivation: reduce manual tuning, improve out-of-the-box cost/perf for Dedicated and Hosted, and provide teams with actionable unit-econ signals to guide model/profile selection. Design summary: 1) batching_defaults service: a runtime component that observes request size distribution and applies a default batch_size_policy and latency SLO target. Config keys exposed: batching_defaults.enabled=true, batching_defaults.min_batch=2, batching_defaults.max_batch=256, batching_defaults.policy=latency_aware. 2) caching defaults: prefix/KV cache TTL and hit-priority heuristics; config keys: cache.autotune_enabled=true, cache.prefix_ttl_default=30s, cache.kv_capacity_policy=adaptive. 3) quant_profiles: YAML-based profiles for 4-bit/8-bit schemes tuned per-arch with conservative-fallbacks; sample profile names: qprofile-gpt2-4bit, qprofile-llama2-8bit. 4) unit-econ tooling: new CLI command redwood uecon report --window=24h and a dashboard endpoint that surfaces cost-per-token, tokens-per-request, and expected marginal cost after batching/caching. Backwards compatibility: all changes opt-in via feature flags and safe defaults are conservative. Tests: unit + integration harness that runs simulated traffic traces (spiky/long-tail/short) against the autotune stack. Related: ENG-8421, PM-559, SUP-1102. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (internal design doc: /docs/design/autotune-uecon.md) - [x] Implementation of batching_defaults and cache heuristics - [x] Quantization profile definitions and tests - [x] CLI + dashboard plumbing for unit-econ reporting - [x] Integration tests with serving runtime - [x] Docs and changelog updates - [x] Metrics and alerting hooks added (uecon.regression, autotune.errors) Notes: this is intentionally conservative; quant profiles include explicit fallbacks to FP16 if a profile results in >1% quality regression on eval set. Deployment plan: enable behind feature flag on main canary, run for 48h, verify uecon metrics, then roll to production clusters via rollout policies.

review_comments: Ethan Kim (reviewer): Overall nice shape. Please add a short section in the design doc about safety valves for quantization regressions. Also note potential mem overhead from keeping per-prefix TTLs.

Aisha Patel (author): Added a 'safety valves' section to docs/design/autotune-uecon.md and implemented a conservative max-memory cap for per-prefix metadata (config key cache.max_prefix_meta_mb). PTAL.
Ravi Singh (reviewer): Integration tests look good but saw a flaky failing test in CI for serving_runtime_tests::TestLargeSequence. Can you re-run and add a retry?
Aisha Patel (author): Re-ran CI after adding a targeted retry in the test harness and added a comment explaining root cause (race in mock clock). Modified test to use deterministic timestamps.
Lena Morozova (reviewer): Approving after minor doc nits fixed. Left one suggestion to expose quant profile names in the model registry UI; not blocking.
Ethan Kim (reviewer): Approved. Left a small suggestion to log when autotune switches policy during runtime for observability. Not blocking.
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and caching, curated quantization profiles with conservative fallbacks, and a new unit-econ reporting CLI/dashboard to help teams evaluate cost/perf tradeoffs. Opt-in via feature flags; no breaking changes.
notes_for_release: Enable behind feature flag; rollout to canary for 48h; monitor uecon.cost_per_token and autotune.errors; follow rollback plan if quality regressions >1% on eval sets.
short_description: Implements autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling to improve out-of-the-box cost/perf and surface tradeoffs to teams.
